title: The Crown Drift, Day-Book, the 9th of Harvest 1012
author: A. Rowse, drift-captain
body:
# Day-book, the 9th of Harvest, 1012

*Deep level broke through at the third hour into a gallery not ours. Square bore, black stone, dry. Ore in it dressed and stacked. Not ours.*

Shift down at the sixth hour to bring it up, by the captain's word and mine:

1. G. Spall, captain
2. T. Pender
3. W. Pender
4. Ezra Hocking
5. Ned Trago
6. Ambrose Vosper
7. Joll Udy
8. Kit Udy
9. Sam Rule, boy

First basket up at the seventh hour. Second at the eighth. Third at the ninth, and full, and nobody on the rope.

*Called down. No answer. Called down. No answer. The board: nine off.*

---

*Below, in a steadier hand, years later:* The Tallymen's clerk came up today and entered the drift closed, no further value. I asked him which column the nine were in. He said there wasn't one.

title: A Weigh-Slate
author: the brass-takers
body:
*Chalk on a roofing slate, the lines wiped and written over:*

PUMP-RODS, 2nd lvl — 4 pig
LADDER-IRONS — 2 pig (DON'T take the ones to the break, Hob)
LAMP PEGS — 1 pig
KIBBLE CHAIN — 3 pig

To the Undercroft man Thursdy: 10 pig @ 4m = 40m
Sayer's cut: 8m. *He says the Hush is 10 now.* He can say it to Hob.

*Underneath, in a different hand:* the green ones were stood at the break again last night, all of them, looking up the winze. Not at us. Up. Nobody go past the plat after the bell.

title: Schedule: the Heronry Eggs
author: the Tallymen's clerk at Sedgehithe
body:
**SCHEDULE OF DUES — THE HERONRY**

*Eggs of the heron, taken at the tower above Sedgehithe, for sale or eating:* one farthing the egg, payable at the taking.

*Eggs counted this day by the undersigned:* —

*Eggs taxed:* —

*In pencil, pressed hard:* NOT ONE. I went up the outside of it as far as the first ledge with the book in my teeth and they came down on me all at once, every one of them, like the sky falling in grey. I have the book. I do not have the hat. Let the Guild send somebody taller.

*Initialled, very small:* J.P.

title: Names, Clean, for Sale
author: a Quiet Hands copyist
body:
*In a careful hand on cheap paper, the columns ruled with a knife's back:*

**No. 2207** — Hobb Tregear, cooper, struck 988 at 31 yrs. *Clean. No kin living.* — 40m

**No. 2650** — Silas Mabe, lighterman, struck 997 at 44. *Clean. A sister in Merrowhithe; won't come.* — 35m

**No. 3118** — Wenna Pascoe, seamstress, struck 1004 at 28. *Clean.* — 40m

**No. 3904** — Amos Pell, carter, struck 1031 at 52. *NOT CLEAN — the daughter chalks him on the Needle every week. Do not sell.*

---

*At the foot:* We copy from the register, never the Needle. The Needle's names are struck. The register's are only numbers, and a number nobody has said aloud in fifty years can be anybody's.

title: A Lead Debt-Weight's Tag
author: the Receiver
body:
*A tag of thin lead on a wire, punched with a clerk's punch:*

No. 3904 · 61 m. 4 s. owing · weighed and found wanting · received

*Scratched on the back with a pin, smaller:* paid 1030, receipt held by the daughter. Entered in error? — Referred to the Tallymen. No reply.

*And under that, in the same hand, newer:* Referred again. No reply. Referred again.

title: The Receiver's Own Entry
author: O. Fenn, Receiver
body:
*A single leaf, ruled as the register is ruled, in the fairest hand in Tollmere:*

**No. 4012** — Obadiah Fenn, Receiver of the Struck, struck 1019 at 67 yrs, the post's fees being owing. Weighed: *not weighed; there is nobody to work the beam.* Received: *not received; there is nobody to receive him.*

Shelved: —

*Under it, the line ruled and ruled again until the pen went through the paper:* Somebody must carry him down.

title: The Creed of the Loud
author: Y. Carrow, once of the Chair of Saying
body:
*Nailed to the reeves' judging-bench, in a lecturer's hand:*

1. The world is going quiet.
2. A thing said loudly is more so. *(The Circle's own first lesson; they have never denied it.)*
3. The Circle teaches its Sayers to say less, and to Hush, and to sell the Hush.
4. Therefore the Circle is making the world quiet, a word at a time, at a fair price.
5. Therefore: louder.

*Under it, in several other hands:* LOUDER. — LOUDER. — *and one, small, near the nail:* my ears hurt all the time now. is that the world getting louder or me

title: The Dues-Roll of the Last Reeve
author: Haskel Mardyke, Reeve of the Mere
body:
# Dues taken at the water-gate, the year of the Charter

*Gullhithe:* eels, two barrels. *Merrowhithe:* smoked pike, forty. *Sedgehithe:* reed, one boatload. *The Holm egg-takers:* one egg, warm, which I did not ask for and do not want.

---

*Below, in the same hand, older:* The Charter is signed. Judging is a service now and has a price, and the Tallymen have priced me at nothing, which I cannot argue with. I have given the keys to the Circle, who want the Saying-hall, and I am going to sit by the north road in my chair and hear what people bring me for free, until they stop bringing it.
